_: THE PRICE LIST. Every number a customer pays lives in this file and nowhere else.
Not in a constant, not in a values file, not in a service. A price in code is a price that
needs a deploy to change, and a price that needs a deploy is one nobody changes — so the real
price list becomes a spreadsheet somebody keeps beside it, and the two disagree within a month.
ci/check_no_prices.py fails the build if 148, 298 or 598 appears in any Python we wrote.
AMOUNTS ARE IN HALALAS and include VAT, because that is what a Saudi customer is quoted: the
shop owner sees 148 and pays 148. amount_minor 14800 is 148.00 SAR.
LIMITS ARE THE PRODUCT. The plan name sells; the limits dict is what actually happens. Three
kinds, and the difference decides who reports the number:
counter  consumed by whoever spends it, reset per period  — messages, custom templates
gauge    the CURRENT value of something owned elsewhere    — seats, branches
boolean  on or off                                          — the features
AND 0 IS NOT ABSENCE. `0` means the key exists and the answer is DENY — which the console can
render as 'your plan does not include this, here is the one that does'. A key that is simply
missing means NOT ENTITLED with no reason to show. Every plan therefore carries every key,
including the zeros, so no surface ever has to guess which of the two it is looking at.
NOTHING ABOUT BRANCHES BEYOND THE COUNT. There is no key for a unified balance and none for
comparing branches: a single balance across branches needs no code at all, and gating it would
mean writing some in order to make the product worse. He is charged for how many branches he
runs, not for them behaving like one shop.
AND WE DO NOT SELL MESSAGES. The establishment contracts with Meta directly and Meta bills it
per delivered message, on a card in its own account — we neither buy them nor resell them, so
selling '1,000 a month' was selling what we do not own. Top-up packs went with it.
messages.monthly SURVIVES AT -1, and the -1 is the whole point: unlimited still INCREMENTS the
counter in billing, so every send is measured and nothing is ever refused for a ceiling of
ours. It is a protection meter — it catches our own runaway loop before the owner's bill does
— and if we ever become a Solution Partner and messages are billed to us, a real number goes
back in this one field and the packs return unchanged.
His actual limit is what WhatsApp allows: 250 unique customers a day before verification,
2,000 after (spec 6.2.2). A second ceiling from us on top of theirs is a number he explains
twice and understands once.

limit_keys.messages.monthly: measured, never sold — see the note above. Uncapped (-1) on every plan
limit_keys.staff.seats: people who can sign in; operations owns the count and reports it
limit_keys.branches: branches; operations owns the count and reports it
limit_keys.feature.insights.engine: the association engine (§10.6) — the one thing nobody else has
limit_keys.feature.roles.custom: building a role of his own, beyond the six we ship
limit_keys.templates.custom: templates he writes himself and we submit to Meta, per month
limit_keys.feature.api: off in every published plan; the key exists so the answer is DENY and not silence

plans.name: الأساسية
_trial: THE TRIAL LIVES HERE, ON THE ENTRY PLAN — not on the middle one, where it started.
A trial on الذكية hands him campaigns and loyalty for two weeks and then takes them away.
The upgrade that follows is bought to stop a loss, and the shop that does not buy feels
downgraded on day 15. On الأساسية the product simply works, and the upgrade comes from a
number in his own dashboard — 340 customers agreed to receive your offers — which is his
fact about his shop rather than a feature we withdrew.
AND THE NUMBER MEANS WHAT IT SAYS AGAIN. Until base-services v0.13.7, trial_days was
written into the subscription and read by nothing: the period end was a full interval
regardless, so 14 days granted 30. It was 0 everywhere while that was true, because a
trial running twice as long as promised is a promise broken in our favour.
0 MEANS NO TRIAL, and the length is set from our panel by editing this row. No service
knows the number, and a shop that signed up under 14 days keeps 14 whatever we change.

_: THE ENTERPRISE SHAPE — priced per conversation, never on the pricing page.
listed=false, so it is invisible to the public plan list and still subscribable. That is
the whole mechanism: a negotiated customer is moved onto this plan from our panel with an
amount agreed with him, and no code anywhere learns that a fourth tier exists.
The amount here is a PLACEHOLDER, not a price. It is what the plan costs when nobody has
negotiated anything, and the panel overwrites it per subscription.
